info.bio:
The Cars fue una banda estadounidense de New Wave proveniente de Boston. Liderada por Ric Ocasek, y conformada además por Benjamin Orr, Greg Hawkes, Elliot Easton y David Robinson, se formaron a mediados de los años 1970 en pleno despegue punk; en 1977 consiguieron un contrato discográfico con Elektra Records y en 1978 lanzaron su primer disco.

El grupo The Cars se creó en 1976 cuando Ric Ocasek y Benjamin Orr se conocieron en una fiesta en Columbus

scenes.name: American Graffiti: revival, garage y power-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: American Graffiti (1973) desata el revival de los cincuenta y sesenta, que suenan más auténticos que el rock corporativo de los setenta: rockabilly, surf, folk-rock, psicodelia, bandas sonoras de terror. Los punks descubren el alma malvada del rockabilly: Suicide inventa el psychobilly y los Cramps el «voodoobilly»; Fleshtones, Raybeats, Stray Cats, Von Lmo. El garage revive con Slickee Boys, Pretenders, Wipers, Real Kids; el power-pop con Cheap Trick, Shoes, Cars, Jonathan Richman y Embarrassment. En California, los Blasters y el cow-punk de Rank And File; Tom Petty como teórico del power-pop, Plimsouls, Redd Kross, Go-Go's, Bangles. El blues para la generación punk: George Thorogood, Fabulous Thunderbirds, J. Geils Band, Dixie Dregs.

podcast.title: New Wave Powerpop
podcast.body: The Cars are identified as one of the new wave bands that embraced Powerpop, integrating its spiky, angular, fun, and sing-along song structures into their sound. They are grouped with other artists who blended punk influences into the Powerpop formula, contributing to its integration into alternative rock. "We had the cars, the shoes, the records, the buzz cocks, Elvis Costello and Joe Jackson."

podcast.body: The Cars were one of many bands from past decades that reunited in the 21st century, a trend largely motivated by financial incentives. With declining CD sales impacting artist revenues, returning to the touring circuit offered a lucrative way to appeal to nostalgic fan bases and fill large venues. "The list of reunions is long."

xref.title: Last Concert (March 1, 1994) – Terminal 1, Munich
xref.body: Nirvana's final performance took place on March 1, 1994, in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany, before an audience of approximately 3,000 people. Kurt Cobain was unwell, suffering from a sore throat, and the performance was not up to par, leading to the cancellation of the remainder of the tour so he could recover from chronic bronchitis and laryngitis. "Nirvana's last ever show was staged in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany on March 1, 1994, in front of about 3,000 people."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Last Concert (Munich, March 1994)
xref.body: Nirvana's final performance was in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany, in March 1994, for just over 3,000 people. The show included a quick acoustic set due to a power failure and a cover of The Cars' "My Best Friend's Girl." "Nirvana's last ever show was held in an airport hangar in Munich, Germany. In March of 1994, in front of just over 3,000 people."

xref.title: Roy Thomas Baker Death (2025) – Producer of Bohemian Rhapsody
xref.body: Roy Thomas Baker, the English producer who guided Queen through their greatest years — including the recording of "Bohemian Rhapsody" — died in 2025 at age 78. He also shaped the distinctive sound of The Cars and worked with artists ranging from David Bowie to Metallica and Guns N' Roses. "Remembered for guiding Queen in their greatest years, including 'Bohemian Rhapsody.'"

xref.title: Extensive Influences
xref.body: Weezer's influences are broad and deep within the Powerpop lineage, including foundational bands like The Beatles, The Ramones, Cheap Trick, The Knack, and The Cars, as well as The Pixies. This wide array of influences supports the argument that they are currently the leading Powerpop band in the world. "Their influences include the Beatles, the Ramones, Cheap Trick, the Nack, the Cars, the Pixies, ensure just about every single band that we've mentioned so far."

xref.title: Influence on Modern Bands
xref.body: Big Star's innovative sound influenced a wide range of bands, from The Cars and Blondie to Sloan and Blink-182, solidifying their legacy as foundational figures in Powerpop. "Someone from the cars in Blondie to Sloan and Blink 1.2 were influenced by Big Star."

xref.title: Influence on Punk and Post-Punk
xref.body: Although Jonathan Richman and the Modern Lovers never achieved significant record sales, they were highly influential to early punk bands and many post-punk groups such as the Sex Pistols, R.E.M., Violent Femmes, Dinosaur Jr., The Cars, The Pixies, and the Ramones. This impact stemmed from Jonathan Richman being a big Velvet Underground fan. "Jonathan Richmond and the Modern Lovers never sold a lot of records, but they were very important to the early punks and many of the post-punk bands like the Sex Pistols and REM and the Violent Femmes and Dinosaur Jr. and the Cars and the Pixies and the Ramones."

xref.title: Musical Influences
xref.body: The Bravery incorporated elements from Depeche Mode, The Cure, Echo & the Bunnymen, The Cars, and Duran Duran to create a sound that felt both new and familiar. Their music, released in 2005, prompted rhetorical questions about whether it was from 2005 or 1980. "They took bits of Depeche Mode, the cure, echo in the bunnyman, the cars, and Durand-Dorand to come up with something new yet very familiar."

xref.title: Post-Breakup Success of Members
xref.body: Following the band's dissolution in 1974, two of its members went on to achieve greater success. Drummer David Robertson found work with another Boston group, The Cars. Keyboardist Jerry Harrison joined the new band The Talking Heads. Both The Cars and The Talking Heads would later become significant components of the American New Wave era. "However, two members of the band went on to bigger and better things. Drummer David Robertson found work with another Boston group called The Cars and Keyboard is Jerry Harrison soon hooked up with a new band called The Talking Heads."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Producer Ric Ocasek's Persuasion
xref.body: Despite Rivers Cuomo's strong reservations, producer Ric Ocasek, leader of The Cars, was adamant about including "Buddy Holly" on the debut album. He, along with the other band members, insisted on its inclusion. Ocasek eventually convinced Cuomo by suggesting they record it, and if Cuomo still disliked it, they could leave it off, but warning him it would be "stupid not to include it." "But Rico Kasek, the leader of the cars and the guy tapped to produce the record, would have none of that."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Producer Selection for Debut Album
xref.body: When asked by Geffen Records who they wanted to produce their debut, Weezer initially boldly suggested they would do it themselves. When pushed for names, someone jokingly suggested Ric Ocasek of The Cars, not expecting it to happen, but Ocasek turned out to be interested. They recorded a practice demo with him on August 11, 1993, and got along great. "Someone in Weezer said, you know, we really like the cars. Get us Ricokasic. That was meant as a joke."

xref.title: Ric Ocasek's Production and Return to Early Sound
xref.body: Ric Ocasek of The Cars produced "Everything Will Be All Right in the End," making it his third and final album with Weezer before his death, having previously produced the Blue and Green Albums. Ocasek was specifically hired to guide Weezer back to their earlier sound. "This was the third and last album to be produced by Rico Cacic of the Cars before he died."

xref.title: Weezer Producer
xref.body: Ric Ocasek of The Cars produced three Weezer albums: the Blue Album, the Green Album, and "Everything Will Be All Right in the End." He was specifically hired for the latter to guide Weezer back to their early sound. He passed away after producing "Everything Will Be All Right in the End." "This was the third and last album to be produced by Rico Cacic of the Cars before he died."
